SecurityPoolFactory

Creates and canonically registers origin and child security pools with their share token, oracle coordinator, and optional Truth Auction. SecurityPoolFactory source contract

Read surface

Use minimumSecurityBondDebtAttoEth and minimumVaultRepDepositAttoRep for immutable deployment floors. Each pool derives its start bond at construction from Zoltar’s universe theoretical REP supply (getUniverseTheoreticalSupplyAttoRep) as max(1 REP, theoretical REP supply / 10,000,000). A zero configured vault REP floor selects the default theoretical REP supply / 100,000; a nonzero constructor value is the exact override. The security-bond debt floor is the exact nonzero constructor value; the repository deployment configuration uses 1 ETH. Construction requires deployed code at both fixed delegate addresses: operations, then accounting/event emitter. Use securityPoolDeploymentCount with the strict securityPoolDeploymentsRange(startIndex, count) pager, which reverts rather than truncating when the requested range exceeds the array. Use getOriginId, getPoolId, getSecurityPool, getSecurityPoolOriginId, and getSecurityPoolHasInheritedForkOutcome for canonical lookup. getPortfolioOriginId includes the portfolio namespace; getSecurityPoolPortfolio and sharedPriceFeeds (indexed by portfolio and universe) identify its owner namespace and shared feed. getChildPoolDependencies returns the coordinator and auction prepared for a parent/outcome pair; a zero coordinator means preparation is still needed. Portfolio children intentionally use a zero auction because their shared fork coordinator owns recapitalization.

State-changing interactions

Each call lists its parameter names in ABI order. The contract index defines the columns.

Transaction Caller Main prerequisites State or asset effect Primary signals
deployOriginSecurityPool(universeId, questionId, statoblastSecurityMultiplierBps, initialReportPriorityFeeAttoEthPerGas) Anyone statoblastSecurityMultiplierBps > 10_001, which makes the halfway migration component strictly greater than one; the effective pool-held vault REP backing multiplier separately floors that component at the 10,500-BPS liquidation-award reserve described by the liquidation design. initialReportPriorityFeeAttoEthPerGas > 0 and remains within the coordinator-computed OpenOracle uint128 report/escalation-halt capacity bound; question exists, the transaction timestamp is strictly before its end time, and it has exactly the categorical labels Yes, then No; universe is unforked and has a REP token; the non-decision threshold exceeds the construction-time start bond max(1 REP, theoretical REP supply / 10,000,000); no pool has already been claimed for this question, multiplier, priority fee, and universe (Security pool origin and universe already claimed). Creates the canonical origin pool, its lineage-wide share token, and its price coordinator with the configured initial-report priority fee, then wires and registers them atomically. SecurityPoolRegistered, then DeploySecurityPool
initializePortfolioPriceFeed(configurationSeed) Anyone, within their own caller-address namespace The seed is a canonical origin ledger in this factory. The feed starts without an accepted price. This call neither registers a question nor allocates REP; a later coordinator must match the feed’s token and priority-fee policy. Creates the caller namespace’s origin-universe feed from a canonical origin ledger’s oracle configuration, or returns its existing feed. Portfolio setup uses this step before the separate first-question admission transaction. Returns the canonical feed address; no question-deployment event.
initializePortfolioPriceFeedForUniverse(configurationSeed, targetUniverse) A portfolio, within its own caller-address namespace Canonical configuration seed; the caller’s logical clock recognizes the target universe; the target REP token exists. The seed may be a standalone pool. Creates or retrieves the caller namespace’s feed for an already registered child universe, using the canonical seed’s oracle configuration. No question needs to be deployed first. Returns the canonical feed address; no question-deployment event.
preparePortfolioPriceFeed(source, targetUniverse) Anyone Canonical portfolio source; the portfolio logical clock recognizes the target; the target REP token exists. Creates or retrieves a target universe feed in the canonical source pool’s portfolio namespace without moving provider capital. Returns the canonical feed address.
deployPortfolioSecurityPool(universeId, questionId, statoblastSecurityMultiplierBps, initialReportPriorityFeeAttoEthPerGas) Anyone, within their own caller-address namespace The ordinary origin deployment checks apply; no lineage for this question/configuration has been claimed in the caller namespace. The namespace is derived from msg.sender and cannot be supplied on behalf of another pool. Creates a separate origin ledger and share token in the caller namespace, attaching its coordinator to the namespace/universe shared REP/ETH feed. Portfolio admission calls this from the portfolio contract, after its immutable admission policy allows the question; it then enforces the question horizon, with failure reverting deployment. SharedPriceFeedSet, feed CoordinatorRegistered, SecurityPoolRegistered, and DeploySecurityPool
preparePortfolioChildPriceFeed(parent, outcomeIndex) Anyone The parent is a canonical portfolio ledger in PoolForked state. Its namespace and oracle configuration determine the feed; Zoltar determines the selected child universe and its REP token. Prepares the child universe’s REP token and shared feed in a separate transaction before creating a portfolio child ledger. Repeated preparation returns the same feed without moving capital or selecting any owner’s migration. Returns the canonical child feed address; child REP deployment may emit Zoltar events.
prepareChildPoolDependencies(parent, outcomeIndex) Anyone The parent is a canonical ledger in PoolForked state. A portfolio must first prepare its child feed. Missing child REP is deployed through Zoltar. The authenticated factory chain exclusively controls subsequent coordinator binding. Predeploys the canonical child coordinator and, for standalone pools only, its Truth Auction, returning the same addresses on repeat calls. This separates their gas cost from child-ledger deployment and dispute continuation. It creates no partial ledger and moves no owner capital. Returns coordinator and auction addresses; no DeploySecurityPool until the child ledger is deployed.
deployChildSecurityPool(parent, shareToken, universeId, questionId, statoblastSecurityMultiplierBps, currentRetentionRate, settlementCollateralAttoEth) SecurityPoolForker only (Only security pool forker) Parent is the canonical pool for its lineage; supplied share token equals the parent share token; no pool has already been claimed for the parent origin in the target universe; a portfolio child feed has already been prepared; deployment arguments satisfy downstream constructors and wiring. Creates and registers a canonical child pool with a coordinator that inherits initialReportPriorityFeeAttoEthPerGas from the parent coordinator and, for standalone pools, a forker-owned Truth Auction, while retaining the parent lineage share token. SecurityPoolRegistered, then DeploySecurityPool
